column1: # ZAP rule configuration for the CI job `dast` (baseline and API scan).
# Format: rule id <TAB> IGNORE|INFO|WARN|FAIL|OUTOFSCOPE <TAB> rule name, or for
# OUTOFSCOPE a regular expression of URLs (Python re.match) the rule does not judge.
# Lines starting with # are comments.
# Rules not listed here are WARN: they show in the reports but do not fail the job
# (the scans run with -I). FAIL is reserved for what the stack already guarantees
# (Caddyfile headers, Django settings) and for injection findings, so a regression
# fails the job. Every IGNORE and OUTOFSCOPE says why.
# Headers the Caddyfile sets on every response (security_headers).

column1: # No CORS grant anywhere: WHITENOISE_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS = False, the API sends none.
# Cookies: Django sets Secure (SESSION_/CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE) and SameSite=Lax.
# Errors and debug output.
# Active scan (API scan only): injection findings are never acceptable.
# IGNORE, each by design:
# 10035: Caddy sends max-age=0 while the server uses its private CA (BRIEVIE_HSTS_SECONDS,
# see the Caddyfile): a browser must be able to pass the certificate warning.
# 10010: the only cookie without HttpOnly is csrftoken (all three alerts of the first
# run). The web app reads it (web/src/api/client.ts) and sends it back as
# X-CSRFToken, so it must be readable. The session cookie is HttpOnly
# (test_the_session_cookie_is_http_only).
# 10112: informational; the "session token" it found is that same csrftoken, which
# identifies no session.
# 10027: matches words like 'user' or 'select' in the minified Vite bundle; there is
# no server-side comment to leak, the bundle is the published AGPL source.
# 10096: matches large numbers in the bundle (constants, hashes) as Unix timestamps.
# 10109: only says the page is a single-page app, which is known.
# OUTOFSCOPE for the web app's paths (everything but /api), judged on /api only:
# 10015, 10049: the web app's files are public and meant to be cached (hashed assets
# for a year, the index revalidated with no-cache). Every /api answer is no-store
# (ApiCacheControlMiddleware) unless its endpoint sets a stricter header.
# 100001: outside /api the server answers with the web app (HTML) or its files (CSS,
# JavaScript), as it should; the API scan expects JSON everywhere.
